title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is from the 'Teichmülleries' notes on dessins and maps (cartes). On the previous page Grothendieck treats the trivial situation (21): the identity Belyi map P^1(C) -> P^1(C) with P^1(R) subdivided barycentrically by 0, 1, ∞. As a map it has one vertex 0, one free half-edge [0,1] whose 'milieu' is 1, and one face centred at ∞. That face f is the sphere slit along [0,1]. Its boundary is the closed edge 0'(1/2)_- 1'(1/2)_+ 0', with single vertex 0' and midpoint 1'. Cutting it by the rays (∞,0') and (∞,1') gives the two flags (repères) r_+ and r_-, which are the upper and lower half-planes.

This page. The problem is to make explicit the canonical conformal (Riemann-mapping) uniformisation of the face of this dessin.
- By the Riemann mapping theorem the open face f is conformally a disc. Normalising centre to centre and vertex to vertex gives a unique isomorphism g: D -> f with g(0)=∞ and g(1)=0'.
- One expects in addition g(-1)=1', g(i)=(1/2)'_+ and g(-i)=(1/2)'_-.

Trick. D is one hemisphere of the standard 'monogone' X_1 = P^1(C). Its map structure is:
- one vertex at 1;
- one edge, the equator, which is a loop through its midpoint -1;
- face centres 0 and ∞ (the polar axis).

The barycentric subdivision of X_1 gives a Belyi map g: X_1 -> X_0 = P^1(C).
- Its degree equals the number of direct flags, which is 2.
- It sends 1 -> 0, -1 -> 1 and {0,∞} -> ∞.
- This exhausts the fibres over 0, 1, ∞. So g is ramified of order 2 over 0 and 1 and unramified over ∞.
- Restricted to the hemisphere |z|<1, g is then the sought conformal map onto the slit sphere.

To compute g, he compares it with the 'analogous' normalised covering g'(z)=z^2 (0->0, ∞->∞, ±1->1). On the next page he composes with Möbius maps:
- ψ(z)=(z-1)/(z+1) and φ(w)=w/(w-1);
- this gives g = φ∘g'∘ψ, i.e. g(z) = -(z-1)^2/(4z) (formula (23)).

Verification:
- On |z|=1, z=e^{iθ}, g = (1-cosθ)/2, which lies in [0,1].
- Point values: g(1)=0, g(-1)=1, g(±i)=1/2, g(0)=∞.
- For z=ir with r<1, Im g = (1/r - r)/4 > 0. So i lands on the upper side (1/2)_+, as predicted.

The point is to give each face of a dessin an explicit canonical conformal model as a standard disc, compatible with its flag decomposition. The notes then move on to the mixed fundamental group Π_{0,3}^τ, which includes complex conjugation.
errors: The monogone's single edge is called 'l'équateur [dans?] P^1(R)'. With 0 and ∞ as poles and 1, -1 on the edge, the equator is the unit circle |z|=1, not P^1(R). This is a slip in wording, or the 'dans' insertion is misread; the mathematics (D = unit disc, boundary maps onto [0,1]) is consistent.

On the next page the intermediate expression is transcribed as ((z-1)/(z+1))^2 / (((z-1)/(z+1))^2 + 1). With φ(w)=w/(w-1) the denominator should be w - 1. The final formula g(z) = -(z-1)^2/(4z) is correct.

ideas.what: Canonical conformal uniformisation of a face of a dessin/map by the unit disc, normalised by centre and vertex (Riemann mapping theorem).
ideas.modern_name: Canonical conformal structure on maps / conformal tilings of dessins
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984); developed by Shabat–Voevodsky (1990, equilateral triangulations) and Bowers–Stephenson (conformal tilings, circle packing)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), section on canonical conformal structure of a map / 'cartes'

ideas.what: Realising the disc as a hemisphere of the 'monogone' map X_1, whose Belyi map to the trivial map X_0 has degree equal to the number of direct flags (here 2), ramified over 0 and 1.
ideas.modern_name: Belyi map of a map from its flag/barycentric data; covering of the trivial dessin
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck; standard dessins d'enfants theory (Jones–Singerman 1978 for maps and triangle groups)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (general principle); this specific computation is unsure

ideas.what: Explicit formula g(z) = -(z-1)^2/(4z), obtained by conjugating z^2 with Möbius maps.
ideas.modern_name: Joukowski-type map: P^1 minus a segment uniformised by the disc

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary, correct worked example: the Joukowski-type map uniformising the slit sphere, interpreted as the degree-2 Belyi map of the monogone. It illustrates the canonical conformal structure of dessins already announced in the Esquisse. Nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'théorie de G[?] représentation conforme' should read 'théorie de la représentation conforme'.
'l'hémisphère positif de la "monogone" standard X_1' is correct. The insertion over 'l'équateur' is uncertain; mathematically the edge is the unit circle.

After 'la ramification est 2 sur 0, 1, et pas de ramification' the elided text presumably says '[sur ∞]'. The following struck-out and inserted words introduce the analogous situation g: P^1(C) -> P^1(C) leading to g'(z)=z^2. The '[?] ... la situation tout à fait analogue' reading is only approximate.
'l'ordre du revêtement est le nb de repères directs, qui est 2': 'directs' is an insertion and is correctly placed.
